verifications.note:
Verified on candidate sha256:45ebccc04d8efc0c4fdc6a842eb3c9ec330bab2ec517b1c592af60b05a066294 (source 7854770e, 544 files). I recomputed it in the working tree and in a disposable clone at 7854770e and at HEAD 041478cb, and tested against disposable PostgreSQL 16 clusters with LANG unset (SQL_ASCII) and with LANG=C.UTF-8 (UTF8).
(1) My round-8 repro, zz-sec-r8-probe.test.ts R6, rerun unchanged, now passes in both runs (round 8: FAIL).
- text/plain with a Content-Length, text/plain chunked (with and without NUL, and valid UTF-8 with a charset): each gives 400 validation.content_type. Nothing is stored and nothing is downloadable. Round 8: 200 with EF BF BD rewrites.
- application/json {"a":1} and [1,2,3]: 400 validation.content_type. Round 8: an undeclared 500 plus an error log.
- application/json "Synthetic": 400. Round 8: 200 with the decoded text stored.
- Control: application/octet-stream, with a Content-Length or chunked, is stored and downloaded byte-exact, with sha256 of the bytes sent.
- No error-level log line.
The same repro over a real socket (r9 S8), chunked, with and without a session: 400 validation.content_type; the octet control gives 200 with an exact sha256.
(2) Code (media-types.ts, server.ts, evidence/routes.ts).
- registerMediaTypeEnforcement runs before any route is registered. It removes Fastify's text/plain parser, adds an onRoute check (assertValidConsumes) and adds one root preParsing hook.
- willParseBody mirrors fastify 5.6.1 lib/handleRequest.js. GET, HEAD and TRACE are bodyless. For DELETE, OPTIONS, PATCH, PUT and POST, the parser runs when there is a Content-Type, or when there is none but there is a Transfer-Encoding or a Content-Length other than 0. 5.6.1 has no OPTIONS exception.
- mediaTypeEssence lower-cases and trims the part before ';', using the same single header value Node passes to the parser (r9 S3: with duplicate Content-Type headers Node keeps the first, and the hook and the parser agree).
- Both parsers are wrapped in restrictParserTo. The JSON parser is still parseAs buffer, followed by createJsonBodyParser and Fastify's defaultJsonParser, so bodyLimit, strict UTF-8 and prototype-poisoning protection are unchanged. R1 to R5 still pass.
- The upload handler refuses anything that is not a Uint8Array or an async iterable without readableEncoding. The 25 MiB streaming limit is unchanged (413 evidence.too_large, media-types.test.ts).
- preParsing runs after onRequest (r9 S7, at a 3/min limit: 400 400 400 429 429) and before the preValidation authentication and CSRF checks, as documented. The contract test asserts consumes = requestBody.content for every routed operation (87 with a body: 86 JSON, 1 octet), and the live sweep sends every undeclared type to every body-carrying operation. Both pass in both locales (contract.test.ts 18/18).
(3) Adversarial probe zz-sec-r9-probe.test.ts:
- S1/S2: case, parameter, quoted-charset, list, wildcard, empty, +json, suffix and parameter-smuggling variants never store rewritten bytes. They never give a 500 and are always declared.
- S4: an absent Content-Type with a body gives 400.
- S6: GET/HEAD bodies are never read, and a request smuggled inside a GET chunked body is not executed. I agree with D-069 (a).
- S4: logout and activateKpiDefinition keep JSON-or-nothing; the handlers never read the body; the web client sends no Content-Type without a body. I agree with D-069 (b).
Two residual Low, non-mandatory observations are raised separately because they are outside this finding's reopen condition: no operation accepts an undeclared media type, and nothing is stored rewritten.
- F-DG2-350: an unmatched route given an application/octet-stream body gives 400 instead of 404, a BE14 regression in restrictParserTo.
- F-DG2-351: a Content-Type whose essence is octet-stream but which Fastify's parser lookup cannot match (a tab before ';') is still the declared 400 and stores nothing, but its detail names application/json. This predates BE14.
This finding's scope and stated remedy are fully fixed.
